# Two inner deepest bases: endpoint cores and an exact paying action

This note is a bounded full-parity probe, principally for n=1,d=2. It does not prove the selected-circuit efficiency assertion for arbitrary four compatible fibers. It proves an endpoint-core sufficient condition without common shape or centroid symmetry, then gives a complete nonaffine four-fiber class with exact critical menus and an actual simultaneous action. The elementary reflected-copy lower bound is archived; the new point here is its two-witness selection and exact response realization.

Throughout, d>=1 unless stated otherwise, mixed mass is the sum of ordinary d-volumes over the four bases 0,1,2,3, and Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d.

## 1. Strict contacts orient every regular critical tilt

Let Y1=(1,y1) and Y2=(2,y2) be two actual globally deepest points of an actual four-fiber family. Suppose each has a regular positive critical circuit, with all continuous normals nonzero and positive total coarea. A proper own trace guarantees the latter. Regular means differentiability of the full cap-mass map in normal and threshold, with the ordinary coarea derivative; positive-area supporting-facet coincidences require separate allocations and are not covered here.

Apply the affine continuous shear

    x'=x-y1-(z-1)(y2-y1).

It fixes all integer bases, has Jacobian one within every fiber, and carries ambient halfspaces bijectively to ambient halfspaces. It makes both selected points (1,0),(2,0).

At source 1 write a critical cap as

    H_j^-={a_j(z-1)+u_j dot x>=0}.

Then a_j<0. At source 2 every critical cap

    H_j^+={b_j(z-2)+v_j dot x>=0}

has b_j>0. This is the archived regular strict-contact lemma: another deepest point is neither inside nor on a regular critical cap. Inside, a threshold increase lowers mass while retaining the second point. On the boundary, the full cap section centroid is the first point by angular stationarity; rotating through the second point in their displacement direction strictly lowers the mass. The positive own coarea makes the loss strict. Evaluation at the other sheared point gives the displayed signs.

A positive continuous-normal circuit at source 1 therefore covers every entire continuous plane over z<=1. The analogous source-2 circuit covers every plane over z>=2. These two covers cover the whole actual integer set. No coverage of the noninteger gap is required.

## 2. Endpoint-core sufficient condition for arbitrary fiber shapes

For a fixed source-1 circuit define its actual left endpoint core

    C_- = int K0 intersect intersection_j (H_j^-)_0.

If C_- is nonempty, there is a nonnegative normal-dependent potential, convex in the full physical variables, localized to the actual left endpoint boundary, with efficiency at least Gamma_d for EVERY normalized nonnegative weighting of this cap list. The analogous statement holds at source 2 using

    C_+ = int K3 intersect intersection_j (H_j^+)_3.

The intersection is with closed cap traces; the chosen point need not lie strictly inside every cap. It must lie in the interior of the endpoint body.

Proof: choose c in C_-. The theorem `candidate 2d9458b5433d0a83` gives one finite positive continuous potential Psi(n,x), convex in x, on K0 at mark c, such that every halfspace containing c receives at least Gamma_d of its weighted boundary measure. This theorem applies at an arbitrary interior mark; c is not asserted to be the ordinary centroid.

Let ell(z)=-z, which exposes base zero. Since the remaining fiber boundaries and normal sphere are compact, a finite B makes

    Phi_-(n,z,x)=[Psi(n,x)+B ell(z)]_+

zero on every other actual fiber boundary. At base zero it equals Psi. This is a genuine finite continuous potential convex in (z,x), so its denominator is the original positive endpoint boundary integral. Every displayed cap contains c at that endpoint. The ordinary theorem and linearity in the weights prove the exact efficiency bound. The proof on the right is the same using ell(z)=z-3.

If both endpoint cores are nonempty, normalize the two potentials to have denominator one and add them. Nonnegativity of all cross contributions gives, for each chosen response profile W_- or W_+,

    integral (Phi_-+Phi_+) W_i deta
       >= Gamma_d,
    integral (Phi_-+Phi_+) deta=2.                         (1)

Thus the single combined potential pays Gamma_d/2 to both selected groups. This is a concrete boundary-response assertion for the actual finite circuits, not an assumption about all critical circuits or all families.

In particular, if the extrapolated common sheared mark 0 belongs to both endpoint interiors, both endpoint cores are nonempty, by the strict tilt signs. This is only a sufficient condition. Neither convex compatibility nor the existence of the two deepest marks has here been proved to force the endpoint-core intersections. The exact class below also shows why requiring the extrapolated mark itself to lie in the endpoints would be unnecessarily restrictive.

## 3. Exact four-fiber family with arbitrary endpoint shapes

Let K be any full-dimensional convex body, V=|K|, with its ordinary deepest point g and maximum raw ordinary halfspace depth q>0. Let A,C be full-dimensional convex bodies satisfying

    A,C subset K intersect (2g-K),
    |A|=|C|=a>0.                                             (2)

The endpoint shapes and centroids may differ. Form the actual convex hull of

    {0} times A, {1} times K, {2} times K, {3} times C.        (3)

Its exact integer fibers are A,K,K,C. Indeed all four continuous sets lie in K, so any combination landing at an inner base remains in K, and the prescribed K is already there. Exposed endpoint fibers are unchanged. Its full projection is [0,3], and it has ambient interior.

**Exact depth theorem.** The two and only two globally deepest mixed points are

    Y1=(1,g),  Y2=(2,g),
    Q=q+a,  M=2V+2a.                                      (4)

For the lower bound at Y1, use A at base zero and its reflected copy 2g-A inside the base-two K. This subsource is centrally symmetric about Y1 and has total volume 2a. Every containing closed ambient halfspace captures at least a from it. The source K contributes at least q. The unused endpoint C contributes nonnegative mass. This proves Q at Y1 for every oblique and pure-integer normal. The reflected C copy in the base-one K proves the same lower bound at Y2.

For any (1,x), choose an ordinary through-x minimum cap of K and use a sufficiently large negative finite integer tilt. It includes all of A strictly, excludes the base-two K and C strictly, and leaves that chosen own trace. Thus

    depth_S(1,x)<=a+depth_K(x).

The analogous positive tilt proves this bound at base two. An endpoint's actual mixed depth is exactly its ordinary depth by finite exposing isolation; in particular it is at most a/2<q+a. These bounds prove the maximum in (4).

For completeness, the ordinary deepest point of a full-dimensional uniform convex body is unique. Its cap mass is continuous over unit normals; at an interior maximum, separation of the compact active gradient set gives a finite positive circuit of critical normals. All own cuts are proper, so their full coarea derivatives exist. A second ordinary deepest point is strictly outside each critical cap by the same regular strict-contact argument as Section 1, contradicting the positive normal dependence. Boundary marks have depth zero. This proves uniqueness and hence the final assertion in (4). Equivalently one may use the archived ordinary instance of that strict-contact theorem.

## 4. Complete regular selected menus

Choose a finite positive ordinary critical circuit at g,

    h_j={u_j dot (x-g)>=0},
    |K intersect h_j|=q,
    sum_j rho_j u_j=0,  rho_j>0.                         (5)

It can have at most d+1 rows, by finite-dimensional convex separation and Caratheodory. Choose one L larger than all absolute values |u_j dot(x-g)| on all four bodies. Then define

    H_j^-={u_j dot(x-g)-L(z-1)>=0},
    H_j^+={u_j dot(x-g)+L(z-2)>=0}.                       (6)

Every H_j^- captures A strictly, cuts only the first K by h_j, and strictly misses the other two fibers. Every H_j^+ captures C strictly, cuts only the second K, and strictly misses the other two. All masses are q+a, so the menus are genuinely globally critical by (4). Their sole proper sections have centroid g by ordinary criticality, and their full mixed centroids are the selected points. All other sections are strictly full or empty. Hence the menus are regular for arbitrary nonsmooth K; no supporting-facet allocation is missing.

The normal circuits in (5) give exactly the two whole-plane covers in Section 1. If S_j>0 is the own coarea factor, their actual response weights are proportional to rho_j/S_j. The conclusions below hold for these weights and indeed for any normalized nonnegative weights on each displayed list.

Every row in the first menu contains the ENTIRE left endpoint, and every row in the second contains the ENTIRE right endpoint. Consequently either source admits an endpoint-localized potential of efficiency exactly one. The endpoint-core criterion holds, even if g is outside both endpoint bodies.

There is a stronger all-critical-menu conclusion when the reflected containments are strict:

    2g-A subset int K,  2g-C subset int K.                   (6a)

Under (6a), EVERY actual critical halfspace through Y1 contains A strictly, and EVERY actual critical halfspace through Y2 contains C strictly. To prove the first statement, the lower bound decomposes its mass into own K mass at least q, paired A/ reflected-A mass at least a, and nonnegative remaining mass. Equality at Q=q+a forces equality in all these bounds.

If its trace on the base-two K had positive volume, that cap would have positive volume outside 2g-A. Indeed a compact set 2g-A inside int K has strictly smaller support in the cutting direction. The positive cap contains a positive-volume portion arbitrarily near K's upper support, outside 2g-A. This makes the paired contribution strictly greater than a, a contradiction. Therefore the base-two cap has zero volume. Its threshold is at least h_K(u). Since h_(2g-A)(u)<h_K(u), every reflected-A point is strictly missed and, by reflection about Y1, every A point is strictly captured. Pure-integer caps cannot be critical: their own contribution is V>q, while the same paired contribution is at least a. The proof at Y2 is identical.

Thus in this strict-core class individual efficiency one holds for ANY regular chosen critical circuit and any normalized response weights, not just the specially selected menus (6). In particular the combined endpoint potential below pays at least one half to any such pair of circuits. The canonical isolating menus still give the exact equalities in (8) and the exact global action formula.

## 5. One exact compatible action, not just two separate costs

Choose c_A in int A and c_C in int C. On the unit continuous normal sphere put

    Phi_A(n,z,x)=[n dot(x-c_A)-B_A z]_+,
    Phi_C(n,z,x)=[n dot(x-c_C)+B_C(z-3)]_+,
    Phi=Phi_A+Phi_C,                                      (7)

where the finite positive constants B_A,B_C are large enough that each summand vanishes on all the other actual fibers. They are genuine globally nonnegative convex physical potentials. On their respective endpoint boundaries their values are the positive radial supports n dot(x-c_A) and n dot(x-c_C).

The divergence theorem gives

    integral Phi_A deta=d a,
    integral Phi_C deta=d a.

The strict endpoint statuses in (6) therefore give

    integral Phi W_- deta = integral Phi W_+ deta=d a,
    integral Phi deta=2d a.                              (8)

The combined efficiency is exactly 1/2 for BOTH groups, simultaneously. For d=2 this is strictly above the requested Gamma_2/2=2/9.

This field realizes an exact actual deformation. Use the canonical concave support roof h_z(n) of the original convex hull and all cuts

    n dot x+epsilon Phi(n,z,x)<=h_z(n).

They define a convex body. At the two middle integer fibers Phi is zero throughout K, so those fibers stay K. At base zero, translate X=x-c_A and H(n)=h_A(n)-n dot c_A>0. The inequalities are precisely

    n dot X+epsilon[n dot X]_+<=H(n),

equivalent to n dot X<=H(n)/(1+epsilon). Thus its actual fiber is

    A_e=c_A+(A-c_A)/(1+epsilon).

The right fiber is analogously C_e=c_C+(C-c_C)/(1+epsilon). There are no extra integer bases. Both new endpoints remain inside the old bodies and hence satisfy (2), with equal volume a_e=a/(1+epsilon)^d.

The same complete depth proof and the SAME finite cap menus consequently give

    Q_e=q+a_e,
    M_e=2V+2a_e,
    beta_e=(q+a_e)/(2V+2a_e).                           (9)

Since q<=V/2<V, beta_e strictly decreases with epsilon. In particular

    beta'_0=-d a(V-q)/(2(V+a)^2)<0.                     (10)

No unproved persistence of a deepest point, free source motion, circuit switch, or exchange of max and derivative is used: (9) solves the full actual family at every epsilon>=0. The action contracts the two physical endpoints together and leaves the two source points deepest throughout.

## 6. A planar rational nonaffine, strictly nonheavy calibration

Take K=conv{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)}, so V=1/2, g=(1/3,1/3), q=2/9. Let

    A=[1/5,3/10] times [17/60,23/60],
    C=[2/5,3/5] times [37/120,43/120].                   (11)

Their areas are both 1/100, but one is a square and the other a rectangle of aspect ratio four. Their centers are (1/4,1/3) and (1/2,1/3); the two middle centers are g. The complete center graph is nonaffine, and there is no common affine center-field symmetry from the archived selection theorem.

The symmetric core K intersect (2g-K) is described by

    0<=x1,x2<=2/3,  1/3<=x1+x2<=1.

Every corner of both rectangles satisfies these inequalities strictly. The mark g belongs to neither endpoint body. Nevertheless the selected finite cap menus and the action above are exact. With the three canonical triangle normals, L=10 is more than sufficient for every strict full/empty status.

The exact global quantities are

    Q=209/900, M=51/50, beta=209/918,
    beta-Gamma_2/2=5/918>0.                            (12)

Every fiber is strictly lighter than M/2=51/100. There are exactly two deepest bases, of opposite parity, and exactly the two displayed deepest points. The potential efficiencies are one separately and one half jointly. Scaling both endpoint bodies down preserves the two deepest points and takes beta to Gamma_2/2 from above.

This is a useful near-target, full-parity calibration of a genuine simultaneous paying action. It is not a counterexample and not a proof for arbitrary compatible unequal middle fibers. The earlier theorem `candidate 24b9a17cce573038` already supplied an OC bound on a larger equal-middle class; the new conclusions here concern exact deepest points, selected critical menus, and their actual combined deformation.

## 7. Remaining arithmetic obligation

For unrestricted compatible K0,K1,K2,K3 with two inner deepest points, strict contact gives the tilt signs but does not here prove that any chosen circuit has a nonempty exposed endpoint core. No common symmetry is available to manufacture a new favorable circuit by orbit averaging. Nor do adjacent opposite-parity marked points by themselves supply an integer-anchored equality to which the T-then-E rigidity theorem applies.

Accordingly, the unrestricted selected-circuit assertion remains separate. Sections 2 and 3–6 are proved sufficient mechanisms with actual geometric hypotheses and actual all-normal calibration; they are not restatements of a conjectural global packing principle.

Supplementary verification: `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_two_inner_deepest_endpoint_action_two_sided.py` passes **2,479 exact checks**, including all rational endpoint vertices, reflected-core containment, actual canonical cap statuses, strict nonheaviness, exact constants, and nested contractions. These checks do not replace the all-normal reflection and isolating-tilt proof.
